event_summary: A disabled passenger launch in the Strait of Varo prompted coordination between Delsa and Namar. Passengers were transferred first, and a later report said all 29 people aboard, including the two crew members, had reached shore in Namar.

timeline_events.time_relation: Before the coordination between the maritime centers and the transfer of passengers.
timeline_events.development: Delsa's patrol station received a distress call reporting that the launch's engine had stopped and the vessel was taking on water.
timeline_events.certainty: Reported by Coastal Signal as information from the caller.

evidence.source_quote: Delsa's patrol station received a distress call from the launch at 04:12. The caller reported that the engine had stopped and the vessel was taking on water.
evidence.attribution: The caller, as reported by Coastal Signal

timeline_events.time_relation: After the distress call; before the reported transfer of passengers at 06:05.
timeline_events.development: Delsa's and Namar's maritime coordination centers agreed on a transfer area.

evidence.source_quote: At 04:38, Delsan and Namar's maritime coordination centers agreed on a transfer area.

timeline_events.time_relation: After the transfer area was agreed; the two crew members were still aboard at this point.
timeline_events.development: Twenty-seven passengers had been transferred, while the two crew members remained aboard as a tow line was attached.
timeline_events.certainty: Reported in a Coastal Signal field update.

evidence.source_quote: At 06:05, 27 passengers had been transferred from the launch; its two crew members stayed aboard while the tow line was attached.

timeline_events.stage: All people from the launch reach shore
timeline_events.time_relation: After the passenger transfer and tow-line attachment.
timeline_events.development: A later report said all 29 people aboard, comprising 27 passengers and two crew members, were ashore at Varo Harbor; the launch was being towed for inspection.
timeline_events.certainty: Reported by Namar Evening Wire, citing the Namar maritime coordination center.

evidence.source_quote: By 06:42, all 29 people aboard the launch—27 passengers and two crew members—were ashore at Namar's Varo Harbor. The Namar maritime coordination center said the launch was being towed for inspection.
evidence.attribution: Namar maritime coordination center, as reported by Namar Evening Wire

source_materials:
Coastal Signal | June 22, 2025, 05:10 local
A passenger launch encountered trouble in the Strait of Varo, between Delsa and Namar. The report stated: Delsa's patrol station received a distress call from the launch at 04:12. The caller reported that the engine had stopped and the vessel was taking on water. At 04:38, Delsan and Namar's maritime coordination centers agreed on a transfer area.

Coastal Signal | June 22, 2025, 06:20 local
A field update stated: At 06:05, 27 passengers had been transferred from the launch; its two crew members stayed aboard while the tow line was attached.

Namar Evening Wire | June 22, 2025, 07:15 local
The report stated: By 06:42, all 29 people aboard the launch—27 passengers and two crew members—were ashore at Namar's Varo Harbor. The Namar maritime coordination center said the launch was being towed for inspection.

cross_report_conflicts.topic: Reported number of people transferred or brought ashore

claims.claim: At 06:05, 27 passengers had been transferred; the two crew members remained aboard while a tow line was attached.
By 06:42, all 29 people aboard, including 27 passengers and two crew members, were ashore.

cross_report_conflicts.resolution_status: Clarified by the later report: the first figure refers to passengers transferred at 06:05, while the later figure includes the two crew members and reports a later time.

event_summary: A rockslide at Kestrel Pass led to a two-way closure of the Lydora–Merova crossing, a joint slope inspection, and the reopening of one lane to escorted traffic. Reports differ on when the closure took effect.

timeline_events.time_relation: Before the reported closure and subsequent inspection.
timeline_events.development: A rockslide covered the eastbound lane at Kestrel Pass.
timeline_events.certainty: Reported by the Eastbank Ledger; no injuries had been reported by 07:00 according to the same report.

evidence.source_quote: At 06:10 local, a rockslide covered the eastbound lane at Kestrel Pass.

timeline_events.event_time: Reported as 06:25 by one source and 06:40 by another, May 14, 2025
timeline_events.time_relation: After the rockslide; before the joint engineering inspection at 10:15.
timeline_events.development: The crossing was closed in both directions. The reports give different times for when the closure took effect.
timeline_events.certainty: Closure reported by both sources; exact time disputed between the reports.

evidence.source_quote: The Lydoran border authority ordered the crossing closed in both directions at 06:25.
evidence.attribution: Lydoran border authority, as reported by Eastbank Ledger

evidence.source_quote: Merovan traffic officials said the two-way closure took effect at 06:40, after loose stones were seen moving above the road.

timeline_events.time_relation: After the closure; before the partial reopening at 16:30.
timeline_events.development: A joint engineering team from the two countries began inspecting the slope.

evidence.source_quote: A joint engineering team from Lydora and Merova began inspecting the slope at 10:15.

timeline_events.time_relation: After engineers removed unstable material; the other lane remained closed afterward.
timeline_events.development: One lane reopened to escorted traffic while the other remained closed pending another inspection.

evidence.source_quote: Engineers removed unstable material, and one lane reopened to escorted traffic at 16:30. The other lane remained closed pending a second inspection on Thursday.

source_materials:
Eastbank Ledger | May 14, 2025, 07:20 local
A rockslide blocked a border crossing between Lydora and Merova. The report stated: At 06:10 local, a rockslide covered the eastbound lane at Kestrel Pass. The Lydoran border authority ordered the crossing closed in both directions at 06:25. No injuries had been reported by 07:00.

Merovan Traffic Bulletin | May 14, 2025, 11:00 local
The bulletin stated: Merovan traffic officials said the two-way closure took effect at 06:40, after loose stones were seen moving above the road. A joint engineering team from Lydora and Merova began inspecting the slope at 10:15. Fourteen trucks were waiting on the Merovan side at 08:30.

Eastbank Ledger | May 14, 2025, 17:10 local
The update stated: Engineers removed unstable material, and one lane reopened to escorted traffic at 16:30. The other lane remained closed pending a second inspection on Thursday.

cross_report_conflicts.topic: Time the two-way crossing closure took effect

claims.claim: The crossing was ordered closed in both directions at 06:25.
The two-way closure took effect at 06:40.

event_summary: Arven and Belor held drought-related water talks at Rovan Dam and signed a protocol on July 3. A trial release was scheduled to begin on July 5. Reports initially differed on whether the signed document was a binding pact; a later joint bulletin described it as a trial protocol that did not change the underlying allocation agreement.

timeline_events.time_relation: Before the document was signed on July 3.
timeline_events.development: Delegations from Arven and Belor began talks at Rovan Dam about drought-related releases from the Sere River.

evidence.source_quote: Talks began at Rovan Dam on July 2.

timeline_events.time_relation: After the talks began; before the scheduled trial release.
timeline_events.development: The delegations signed a document concerning a 30-day water release. Reports characterized its legal status differently, and a later joint bulletin described it as a trial protocol that did not alter the underlying allocation agreement.
timeline_events.certainty: The signing is reported by multiple sources; the document's status is characterized differently across reports and later clarified by the joint bulletin.

evidence.source_quote: At 09:30 on July 3, the delegations signed a binding 30-day release pact.
Arven's water commissioner said the document signed at 09:30 was an interim operating protocol, not a treaty, and required domestic approval before any permanent allocation changes.

evidence.source_reference: Joint Water Desk Bulletin, July 4, 2025, 08:00 local
evidence.source_quote: The two water agencies said the signed protocol authorizes a trial release of 18 cubic meters per second from July 5 through August 4. It does not alter the countries' underlying allocation agreement and remains subject to approval for any permanent change.

timeline_events.time_relation: Scheduled after the July 3 signing; the joint bulletin describes the trial period as running through August 4.
timeline_events.development: A trial release of 18 cubic meters per second was authorized by the signed protocol, according to the later joint bulletin.
timeline_events.certainty: Scheduled and reported; the source materials do not confirm that the release subsequently began.

evidence.source_quote: The first release is scheduled for July 5 at 06:00.

evidence.source_reference: Joint Water Desk Bulletin, July 4, 2025, 08:00 local
evidence.source_quote: The two water agencies said the signed protocol authorizes a trial release of 18 cubic meters per second from July 5 through August 4.

source_materials:
Borderline Gazette | July 3, 2025, 12:10 local
Delegations from Arven and Belor met at Rovan Dam to discuss drought-related water releases from the Sere River. The report stated: Talks began at Rovan Dam on July 2. At 09:30 on July 3, the delegations signed a binding 30-day release pact. The first release is scheduled for July 5 at 06:00.

Arven Public Radio | July 3, 2025, 12:45 local
The report stated: Arven's water commissioner said the document signed at 09:30 was an interim operating protocol, not a treaty, and required domestic approval before any permanent allocation changes.

Joint Water Desk Bulletin | July 4, 2025, 08:00 local
The bulletin stated: The two water agencies said the signed protocol authorizes a trial release of 18 cubic meters per second from July 5 through August 4. It does not alter the countries' underlying allocation agreement and remains subject to approval for any permanent change.

cross_report_conflicts.topic: Legal status and effect of the signed water-release document

claims.claim: The delegations signed a binding 30-day release pact.
The document was an interim operating protocol, not a treaty, and required domestic approval before permanent allocation changes.

cross_report_conflicts.resolution_status: Clarified by the July 4 joint bulletin: the document authorized a trial release and did not alter the underlying allocation agreement; permanent changes remained subject to approval.
